description: A pulse oscillator built as two 555 timer chips would be wired, one running free and triggering the other, whose pulse length is set in milliseconds rather than as a fraction of the cycle

params.text: Sets the frequency of the free-running oscillator, four octaves either side of C4
Sets how long the output stays high after each trigger, 0.1ms to 20ms, which changes the timbre without changing the rate

inputs.text: Shifts the frequency by 0.8 octaves per volt, added to the frequency knob and clamped to four octaves either side of C4; it does not track a volt per octave
Lengthens the output pulse by 2ms per volt, added to the pulse-length knob and clamped between 0.1ms and 20ms

outputs.text: The rectangular wave, switching between -5V and 5V

notes: a trigger arriving during an output pulse is discarded rather than lengthening it, so with the pulse longer than the oscillator's period the rate is governed by the pulse length, not the knob
nothing on the panel is lettered; the artwork carries the module name and no control labels at all

inputs.0:
±5V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
inputs.1:
